summary: Analysis of 14 days of telemetry data shows exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), and a low Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Overnight fasting glucose is remarkably stable (102-108 mg/dL). Baseline basal rates, ISF, DIA, and carb ratios are accurately set. The primary area for optimization is prebolus timing during weekend brunch to mitigate mild postprandial peaks (up to 188 mg/dL) without altering underlying profile parameters.

analysis_steps.findings: 100% CGM coverage over 14 days (1,345/1,345 entries) with no gaps exceeding 15 minutes. Active AAPS profile and 28 logged meal treatments are fully intact.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries at 15-minute cadence; 0 gap count; active profile ID 950d0da5-fd1d-4fdc-8a12-298fa1671fd1.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic variability is exceptionally low (CV 12.9%, SD 15.1 mg/dL) with zero recorded hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) and minimal time above range (0.3%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL; TIR 99.7%; TAR 0.3%; TBR 0.0%; minimum glucose 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain flat glucose levels within target range without requiring excessive automated closed-loop corrections or dipping.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight hourly local glucose averages stay between 102.3 and 107.5 mg/dL from 00:00 to 05:00 local time on a 0.85 U/h basal rate.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile CRs at 06:00 (10 g/U) and 18:00 (9 g/U) perform effectively. Weekend brunch CR (11 g/U) displays a postprandial rise up to 188 mg/dL that resolves smoothly by 4-6 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast 2h rise +33 to +57 mg/dL with 4h return; dinner 2h rise +15 to +41 mg/dL; weekend brunch 2h rise +62 to +70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM settings operate cleanly without stacking insulin or causing post-meal hypoglycemia. Delivery intervals and max basal minutes are appropriately set.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true; smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min.
data_gaps: Raw export contains null values for specific smb_activation conditions.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8 U) are safely scaled to scheduled parameters. Automation is not compensating for underlying profile defects.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal 2.4 U/h vs max scheduled basal 1.05 U/h; max IOB 8.0 U vs max scheduled bolus 5.8 U.
data_gaps: Autosens toggle states are null in exported raw settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Prebolus timing of 20 minutes for fast-carb breakfasts yields excellent outcomes. The 10-minute prebolus for weekend brunch allows a pronounced initial spike.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast postprandial 4h delta +1 to +8 mg/dL; weekend brunch postprandial 2h peak up to 188 mg/dL (+70 mg/dL rise).

analysis_steps.findings: Declaring 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes for weekend brunch effectively prevents late-window stacking while glucose safely returns to baseline by 4-6 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunch 4h delta -11 to +1 mg/dL; 6h delta -5 to -15 mg/dL; 0.0% TBR across period.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA) and AAPS safety limits are well-matched. No profile changes are recommended. Optimization focus is limited to extending prebolus timing for weekend brunch.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesized 14-day TIR of 99.7% with 0% TBR across all 1,345 CGM readings and 28 meal entries.

recommendations.title: Extend Prebolus Timing for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Extend prebolus timing for weekend brunch from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes prior to eating. This addresses 2-hour postprandial peaks (up to 188 mg/dL) without increasing carb ratios or risking late hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Verify On-Device SMB and Autosens Toggles
recommendations.description: Review AAPS raw settings on the device to explicitly verify SMB activation conditions (e.g., smb_with_cob_enabled) and Autosens toggles that were unpopulated in the export file.

profile_recommendation.next_check: Conduct a trial of 15-20 minute prebolus timing for weekend brunch while keeping all profile settings constant.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain baseline prebolus timing (15-20 min) and split bolus/e-carb strategies for routine meals. Extend weekend brunch prebolus timing to 15-20 minutes while retaining the 60% upfront bolus and 20g e-carb distribution.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: TIR of 99.7% confirms overall meal strategy efficacy. Weekend brunch peaks (188 mg/dL) stem from rapid early carb absorption under a brief 10-minute prebolus rather than an incorrect CR.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor 2-hour postprandial peak glucose during weekend brunch following a 15-20 minute prebolus trial.

exceptions.suggestion: Increase prebolus time from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes while keeping 60% immediate bolus and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Mitigates the 2-hour spike of 188 mg/dL (+70 mg/dL rise) while maintaining safe descent without late hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: Verify null AAPS settings (SMB activation conditions and Autosens toggles) directly on your device.
Maintain all active profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, and targets) as currently configured.
Test extending prebolus timing for weekend brunch meals from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes.
Observe 2-hour postprandial glucose peaks over 2-3 weekend brunch cycles to confirm peak reduction before evaluating any further adjustments.
education: A Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range demonstrates excellent alignment between baseline insulin settings and body requirements.
Postprandial peaks following high-fat or mixed meals are often caused by timing mismatches between fast early carb absorption and insulin action, rather than an incorrect carb ratio.
Adjusting prebolus timing or using extended carbs helps flatten postprandial peaks without introducing late-window hypoglycemia risk.
safety_notes: This analysis provides decision-support information only and does not constitute medical advice.
Independently verify all proposed strategy adjustments with your diabetes healthcare team.
Make adjustments one at a time and monitor glucose closely following any procedural change.
